summary: Taking sequencing data from raw reads to results: PhIP-Seq enrichment analysis ([phippery](https://jaredgalloway.com/research/#phippery)), deep mutational scanning, and phylogenetic analysis of 13M+ viral genomes. Public Nextstrain views support genomic surveillance of SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and Lassa virus.

Transformer models of viral protein evolution (DASM, in PyTorch), joint models of deep mutational scans ([multidms](https://jaredgalloway.com/research/#multidms), in JAX), neural-network global epistasis models (torchdms, in PyTorch), and recurrent networks for recombination-rate estimation ([ReLERNN](https://jaredgalloway.com/research/#relernn), in TensorFlow/Keras).
Pulling biological signal out of noisy experiments with sparse regularized models, global epistasis, and Bayesian methods. Simulation supplies the training data and validates each method.
Python for nearly everything; C++ for tree-sequence recording in the SLiM simulator; R, Bash, and JavaScript where a project called for them; SQL from computer science coursework.
Wrangling and encoding large biological datasets, from phylogenies of 13M+ viral genomes to multidimensional PhIP-Seq data.
Figures for papers in *Cell* and *eLife*. Interactive tools include [phippery](https://jaredgalloway.com/research/#phippery)'s Streamlit app and multidms's plots.

Reproducible pipelines in Nextflow and Snakemake (one ran 50K+ jobs on an HPC cluster), built on Docker or Apptainer containers with GitHub Actions for CI. Sensitive-data management on HPC file systems and AWS S3.
